question: In progressive hyperkalaemia, peaked (tall, narrow, symmetrical) T-waves appear before PR prolongation and QRS widening on the ECG.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Peaked T-waves are the earliest ECG manifestation of hyperkalaemia, occurring at potassium approximately 5.5–6.5 mEq/L. PR prolongation and QRS widening develop at higher potassium levels. Recognising this sequence is essential for risk stratification.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The ECG changes of hyperkalaemia follow a characteristic sequence with rising potassium: (1) peaked T-waves (K⁺ ~5.5–6.5) → (2) PR prolongation and P-wave flattening (K⁺ ~6.5–7.0) → (3) widened QRS (K⁺ ~7.0–8.0) → (4) sine-wave pattern → (5) ventricular fibrillation/asystole. Peaked T-waves are the earliest and most consistent ECG sign.
